title: Reactive Relapse
summary: Relapse is expected under pressure — triggers + protection rules + AI monitoring

sections.heading: Orientation — Lesson Start
sections.subtitle: Lesson Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What will you understand? Even after building a system, pressure can push you back into Reactive Mode — and AI helps you monitor signals and summarize warnings.
- Why now? You have built a rhythm and SOP (Standard Operating Procedures) and thought about expansion. Relapsing is more dangerous when you feel like you’re «done».
- What after the lesson? You will identify the top triggers for relapse and a protection rule for each.

sections.heading: Tension — Familiar Situation
sections.subtitle: Familiar Situation
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Two weeks of a good system — then a successful campaign, a major complaint, or cash pressure — and suddenly you are back in reactions and firefighting.
- Reactive Relapse is not a moral failure — it’s a signal that a pressure trigger has broken through your protection.
- Common triggers: Sudden growth, team gaps, recurring complaints, cash pressure. AI summarizes the week and asks you, «What has increased beyond normal?»

sections.heading: Core Idea — Monitor the Trigger — Not Just «Be Disciplined»
sections.subtitle: Monitor the Trigger — Not Just «Be Disciplined»
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Relapse starts small: You open a message saying «Just this one» before the strategy block — then the whole day is Reactive.
- A protection rule is simple and actionable: «No WhatsApp before 9:30» or «Any major complaint → AI draft + response after an hour».
- AI helps you weekly: summarize customer complaints, count messages, identify a recurring theme — an early signal before you drown.

sections.heading: Glossary — Key Terms
sections.subtitle: Key Terms
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---------|--------|------|
| Reactive Relapse | Returning to managing the day with reactions and crises after a period of system — due to a pressure trigger | After product launch: 3 days of reactions only — strategy block disappeared |
| SOP (Standard Operating Procedures) | Agreed-upon steps that reduce improvisation under pressure | «Any major complaint → AI draft then response after an hour» |
| AI monitoring | A weekly question for AI that summarizes signals before you drown | «What is the recurring theme in this week’s complaints?» |

sections.heading: Quiz — Quick Confirmation

sections.contentMarkdown:

Leave the system completely — sales are more important.
Identify the trigger, use AI to summarize, and apply one protection rule.
Hire immediately without SOP.

sections.heading: Mission — Two Triggers + Protection Rule
sections.subtitle: Two Triggers + Protection Rule
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: Think about the last time you felt you went Reactive (or close to it). Identify your top two triggers — and write a simple protection rule for each. Not a lifelong promise — rules you can implement next week. Delivery: 1. Relapse Trigger #1
2. Protection Rule #1
3. Relapse Trigger #2
4. Protection Rule #2
5. One question you will ask AI every week for monitoring Mission Template: ```
1) Trigger 1: [Example: Cash pressure] 2) Rule 1: [Example: Review cash every Monday before any large spending] 3) Trigger 2: [Example: Recurring complaints] 4) Rule 2: [Example: AI summarizes complaints on Friday] 5) Weekly question for AI: [Write here]
``` Evaluation Criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Real Triggers | 60% | Two triggers from your experience — not a general list |
| Actionable Rules | 40% | Two simple rules + weekly monitoring question |
